title: helm(private): tighten values schema + add init-hook for v1.8 upgrades, templating and rollback compatibility
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Fix: stricter values schema for private installer; Add: pre-upgrade init hook job to populate CRDs and secrets for v1.8; Fix: templating edge-cases for toYaml and multiline KMS configs; Improve: upgrade/rollback compatibility to avoid failed rollbacks caused by init-job name collisions.
description:
Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private have seen upgrade failures when moving to v1.8 due to missing CRDs/secrets and more permissive values acceptance in the Helm chart. This PR tightens the values.schema.json, fixes templating edge-cases, and adds an opt-in pre-upgrade init hook job that ensures required CRDs and bootstrap secrets exist before the main upgrade proceeds. The change also includes compatibility work to make rollbacks safer (avoid leftover hook jobs causing chart collisions) and smaller fixes to helper templates used by the private installer.

What this changes: 1) values.schema.json: - Added explicit schemas for networking.vpc, kms (key_id | kms_provider), storage.backend and storage.size to fail fast on invalid configs. - Added deprecations for legacy fields that were accepted previously (networking.publicSubnet -> networking.subnets). 2) templates/init-hooks/pre-upgrade-bootstrap.yaml: - New Helm hook (pre-upgrade, pre-install) job that creates CRDs, ensures KMS encryption keys are referenced, and creates initial bootstrap secrets required by on-prem deployments. - Job is opt-in via values.private.initHooks.enabled (default: false for existing installs). 3) templates/_helpers.tpl and legacy helpers: - Fixed toYaml usage with default empty maps to prevent nil rendering for absent configs. - Added helper for stable hook job names to avoid collisions between releases. 4) Chart tests and CI: - Added a helm unittest case to cover values schema validation and a smoke integration job in CI that runs the pre-upgrade hook flow in KinD.

Upgrade notes: - For clusters upgrading to v1.8, enabling values.private.initHooks.enabled=true is recommended for a one-time pre-upgrade run to bootstrap CRDs and secrets. The hook is designed to be idempotent; it will no-op if resources already exist. - The schema is intentionally stricter: users with legacy fields will see validation errors; migration instructions are included in the release notes.

Rollbacks: - Implemented stable hook naming and a cleanup path for pre-upgrade jobs to prevent Helm from failing rollbacks when jobs remain in the cluster. The hook uses finalizers and a short TTL to ensure automatic cleanup if installs abort.

Testing and CI: - Unit tests: helm lint + helm unittest added. - Integration: KinD job exercises install -> pre-upgrade hook -> upgrade -> rollback path. - Manual QA: tested against a small on-prem cluster with KMS mock and against AWS VPC-like network config.

Related: Linear ENG-1253 tracks the long-term schema migration plan; SUP-441 is the customer support ticket that drove the initial investigation.

Checklist: - [x] values.schema.json updates - [x] new init hook templates - [x] helper template fixes - [x] tests added and CI green - [x] documented upgrade path in release notes
commits:
1) tighten(values): update values.schema.json to validate kms/network/storage fields
2) feat(init-hooks): add pre-upgrade bootstrap job template (opt-in)
3) fix(templates): toYaml nil guard and stable hook name helper
4) test(ci): add helm unittest + kind integration job
5) docs(release): add upgrade notes for v1.8

Jonah Kim: Helm hook name collision was causing failed rollbacks in earlier runs, can we add deterministic naming? — replied: Maya Patel: added stable-name helper and included the release.Revision to avoid collisions.

notes_for_operators: - If you run a self-hosted installer: enable values.private.initHooks.enabled=true for a controlled pre-upgrade run. - If your CI pins helm chart versions, update schema-aware validation to accept new required fields or use the provided migration snippet in charts/redwood-private/README.md. - Rollbacks should be safer: if you still see job collisions, delete pre-upgrade hook jobs that match label redwood-preupgrade and re-run helm rollback.
human_readable_summary: This PR tightens the Helm values schema for the redwood-private chart, adds an opt-in pre-upgrade init hook to bootstrap CRDs and secrets for v1.8 upgrades, fixes templating edge cases, and improves rollback compatibility. It includes tests and CI updates and has been merged into main.
